flawed_step: Line 0002 falsely claims that the objects of CLat form a subcollection of the objects of Frm.
counterexample: Let M3 be the five-element diamond lattice {0,a,b,c,1}, where a,b,c are pairwise incomparable atoms. Being finite, M3 is a complete lattice, so it is an object of CLat. But it is not a frame: b∨c=1, hence a∧(b∨c)=a, while (a∧b)∨(a∧c)=0∨0=0. Thus finite meets do not distribute over arbitrary joins, so M3 is not an object of Frm.
assessment_summary: The required inclusion of objects fails, so CLat is not a subcategory of Frm under the stated standard definitions.
